name: Kashu Yamazaki

papers.title: VLM-Guided Contact Retargeting and Generative Partner Modeling for Deployable Humanoid-Human Interaction
papers.abstract:
Humanoids are advancing toward sharing everyday spaces with people, yet reactive humanoid--human interaction (HHI) remains an open question because existing controllers either treat the robot in isolation or engage only static objects and scenes. HHI is challenging because handcrafting an interaction reward is complicated, noisy two-human motion-capture demonstrations cannot be retargeted onto a humanoid without losing their inter-person contacts, and on-board close-range perception breaks down under occlusion and out-of-view human subjects. We present REACT, a learning pipeline that scales HHI to a large corpus of human--human demonstrations. It uses a vision-language model to detect plausible spatio-temporal contacts, and a contact-preserving retargeting stage maps each demonstration onto the humanoid--partner geometry. A privileged-state teacher trained with an interaction contact reward is then distilled into an ego-depth student, with a realistic human partner rendering in the loop so that training-time depth matches the deployed sensor. We also use generative human-pose-estimation auxiliary loss to handle the multimodality of close-range perception.
On a real Unitree G1, REACT executes diverse, contact-rich interactions with a human partner, significantly outperforming a baseline that relies on an external pose-estimation module, which becomes inaccurate at close range.

papers.title: ExtremControl: Low-Latency Humanoid Teleoperation with Scaled Velocity Feedforward
papers.abstract: Building a low-latency humanoid teleoperation system is essential for collecting diverse reactive and dynamic demonstrations. However, end-to-end latencies in existing approaches consistently hover around 200ms, roughly equal to human reaction time, that severely limits responsiveness and prevents tasks requiring rapid feedback. We identify position-only PD control as the root cause of this latency floor and propose ExtremControl, a low-latency whole-body control framework that: (1) incorporates scaled velocity feedforward in low-level control, reducing tracking delay by approximately 70ms with a provably optimal feedforward ratio; (2) operates directly on SE(3) poses of selected rigid links, primarily humanoid extremities, to avoid joint-space retargeting in the control loop. To minimize retargeting time, we derive a closed-form Cartesian-space mapping that uses a single anthropomorphic calibration step to translate human motion into humanoid link targets, accommodating operators with varying body proportions. Furthermore, we provide a theoretical framework for selecting control hyperparameters, and validate the effectiveness of velocity feedforward control in the reinforcement learning for locomotion setting through experiments in both simulation and the real world. Building on ExtremControl, we implement a teleoperation system supporting both optical motion capture and VR-based tracking, achieving end-to-end latency as low as 50ms --- well beneath the threshold at which system delay adds a full human reaction cycle to the control loop. This enables a qualitatively new class of reactive behaviors, including ping-pong ball balancing, juggling, and real-time return, that are beyond the capability of existing teleoperation systems.
